failure_summary.description: Every trajectory left at least one result-producing call without assigning and saving its result to cache.
Agents re-searched instead of refining a compatible cached result, or retrieved a result without applying the new constraint.
Agents treated the latest reply as the whole request and omitted an earlier domain or a distinct return leg.
Agents omitted or mis-mapped explicit constraints, including a non-stop request and a hotel party-size field.

patch.reasoning: The batch repeatedly shows a gap between general instructions and executable call planning: results are not saved, new constraints are not actually applied to cached objects, and follow-up replies cause earlier work or flight legs to be dropped. A full-request checklist and more explicit call contracts address these repeated omissions; a brief schema mapping rule covers the remaining explicit-field errors.

edits.content: - Before planning, enumerate all still-active requested actions from the full conversation, including each requested domain/item and each one-way flight leg. Treat a reply to an assistant follow-up as filling or refining the plan, not replacing earlier requests. For every checklist entry, identify valid cache satisfaction, a needed refinement/search, or missing mandatory information; do not finish with an uncovered entry. Apply a direction-neutral flight preference to each applicable leg separately.

edits.target: - When refining a cached result, do not resend criteria already represented in that result; apply the newly introduced preference with the appropriate filter.
edits.content: - For a new constraint on a cached result, retrieve a compatible listed cache key into a local variable and pass that exact object as `prior_results` to the matching filter. Include each newly introduced, schema-supported constraint as its named filter argument: passing only `prior_results` or merely retrieving the result does not apply the constraint. Save the filtered output under a new key. If no compatible base exists, search when mandatory inputs are available.

edits.target: - Bind the exact return value of every search, filter, sort, and nearest-results call to a variable, then save it with `save_to_cache` under a unique, descriptive key. Save refined results under a new key. Do not substitute hand-built dictionaries or redefined models for tool result objects.
edits.content: - Treat every result-producing call as an indivisible sequence: assign the exact return value of each search, filter, sort, or nearest-results call to a local variable, then immediately save that same object with `save_to_cache` under a unique, descriptive key before proceeding. Do this for every call, including each flight leg and each refinement; never leave a result-producing call bare or overwrite a base-result key with a refinement. Do not substitute hand-built dictionaries or redefined models for tool result objects.

edits.target: ## Validate tool arguments and preserve user intent
edits.content: - Map an explicit “non-stop,” “direct,” or “no stops” flight request to `num_layovers=[0]` for each applicable leg. For hotel calls, map an explicitly stated people count to `num_people` and a stated room count to `num_rooms`; keep these fields separate.
